merger_description:
This notification waiver application relates to the proposed indirect joint acquisition of the entire share capital and voting rights in DCC Energy plc (**DCC**) by Krypton Holdco II Limited (**Krypton Holdco**) and ECP Dragon Holdco Ltd (**ECP Dragon**) (together, the **Acquirers**), through their jointly owned special purpose vehicle Dragon Bidco Limited (**Dragon Bidco**) (the **Acquisition**).

Dragon Bidco is a special purpose vehicle with no prior business activities which has been established for the purpose of the Acquisition.

Krypton Holdco is a special purpose vehicle indirectly wholly owned by investment funds, vehicles and/or accounts advised and managed by various subsidiaries of KKR & Co. Inc. (**KKR & Co.**, and together with its subsidiaries, **KKR**). KKR is a global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit, and real assets and has strategic partners that manage hedge funds.

ECP Dragon is a special purpose vehicle indirectly wholly owned by investment funds, vehicles, and/or accounts respectively advised and/or managed by affiliates of Energy Capital Partners (**ECP**), a private equity firm founded in 2005 which acquires and invests in a range of energy infrastructure-related assets, which was acquired by Bridgepoint Group plc (**Bridgepoint**) in 2024. Bridgepoint is active in private asset growth investing across private equity, infrastructure, private credit, and secondaries.

DCC is a multi-energy sales and distribution group headquartered in Dublin and listed on the London Stock Exchange. DCC operates worldwide through two divisions: DCC Energy, its principal division, a downstreammarketer and distributor of energy products and services in North America and Europe, and DCC Technology (trading as Nexora), a value-added distributor of professional technology solutions throughout North America and Europe. In Australia, DCC Energy’s operations are limited to the supply of lubricants to Australian customers.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given there is no horizontal overlap or
vertical relationship between DCC and KKR or Bridgepoint (or their
connected entities) in the supply of lubricants or professional
technology solutions in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
